JOINT EVALUATION TEST 2026
 101/1
 ENGLISH
 MARKING SCHEME
 1. MINUTES (20 MARKS)
 a. FORMAT -6mks
 i. TITLE - √ 1mk
 ATTENDANCE
 √ Present - ½ mk
 √ Apologies - ½ mk
 √ Absent - ½ mk
 √ In Attendance - ½ mk
 ii. PRELIMINARIES ½ MK
 iii. CONFIRMATION OF PREVIOUNS MINUTE ½ MK
 iv. MATTERS ARISING
 v. A.O.B ½ mk
 vi. ADJOURMENT ½ mk
 vii. SIGNING OFF
 √ Secretary _________________ Sign_________________ Date ___________ ½ mk
 √ Chairman ________________ Sign _________________ Date ___________ ½ mk
 b). CONTENT
 ✓ Preliminaries - Opening remarks - * P1
 ✓ Confirmation of Previous Minutes - *C 2
 ✓ Matters Arising - *M1
 ✓ Recruitment of new members * A1
 ✓ Science Day *As1
 ✓ Election of Officials * E1
 ✓ A. O. B * O1`
 Total Marks = 08 marks
 c). LANGUAGE
 GROUP D (01 – 02)
 Candidate does not communicate and their language is so minimal that the examiner has to guess what
 they intent to write.
 ✓ Poor use of expressions
 ✓ Poor use of punctuation marks
 ✓ Hardly any correct sentence
 ✓ Spelling errors
 ✓ Broken parts must be identified
 GROUP C (03 – 04)
 ✓ Lack of confidence
 ✓ Very simple sentences
 ✓ All manner of broken sentences
 ✓ Mother tongue interference
 ✓ Errors of tense and construction
 ✓ Subject verb agreement
 GROUP B (05)
 ✓ Communicates fluently with ease of communication
 ✓ Well – constructed sentences
 ✓ Good use of vocabulary
 ✓ A few errors considered as slips
 GROUP A (06)
 ✓ Ease of expression with no errors of punctuation, spelling and grammar
 ✓ Good planning/organization of ideas
 ✓ Clever use of vocabulary and maturity in language use.
 ✓ Definite spark.
 NB: IT MUST BE MINUTES. IF NOT -2AD WRONG FORMAT
 ❖ Mixed format - 1AD MF
 ❖ The Title must have the following items to earn (Minutes, Name of Club, Date, Time, Venue
 and Time of Meeting.)
 ❖ Attendance should have the given number of names and titles to earn marks. If it exceeds or is
 less, do not award.(should be numbered)
 ❖ Confirmation of previous minutes should indicate who read (secretary), who proposed and who
 seconded(full name)
 ❖ Matters Arising should capture the minute under reference and the response given.
 ❖ The substantive matters must be discussed and resolved or agreed to earn a mark. A mention of
 the issue under deliberation without agreement should not be awarded.
 ❖ The elections must be conducted and names of new officials given. Alternatively, the candidate
 may state that the current officials we re-elected unanimously.
 ❖ The minutes should be captured in the past tense and continuous prose.
 ❖ It should be third person passive voice/impersonal active voice.
 ❖ A.O.B should just be mentioned and not discussed.
 ❖ Adjournment should indicate the end of deliberations and a possible date of the next meeting.
 2. CLOZE TEST

 2. ill

 3. ORAL SKILLS
 a. Narrative
 (i). Preparation for delivery of an oral narrative
 (Answers should be personalized e.g. I would….)
 ✓ Prior recitation before the day of performance in order to master the content.
 ✓ Have prior information about the audience
 ✓ Prepare appropriate costumes and accompaniments
 ✓ Stage a mock narration before an imaginalry audience in order to boost confidence
 ✓ Choose conventional/standard ways of attracting the attention of the audience;
 clapping of hands, clearing throat etc.
 ✓ Practice the use of facial expressions, tonal variation and gestures.
 (ii). MUST BE ILLUSTRATED IF NOT NO MARK.
 Opening formula
 - Closing formula
 - Direct address to audience e.g like all of.
 - Direct translation “It came to a time’
 - Timelessness
 - Hyperblole “Fetch me a whole river of water.
 “ dig the whole shamba
 - Use of proverbs - something doesn’t always fall where it is thrown.
 - Use of conversational words - ----just like all of you good children, eh.
 --- just as you will grow, good children
 - Use of rhetorical question “Do you know what strange thing happened?
 (iii). Use of hyperbole (1 mk)
 That the girl is told to fetch a whole river of water or dig the whole shamba.
 vi)- Pauses and Commas/Dramatic pauses.
 -Stress on content words – such as children, evil, pay
 -Use hand gesture 0 paint at the audience
 -Maintain eye contact with children at the audience.
 b). i). Gore
 (ii). Ambush
 (iii). Exile
 iv). Gate
 c). SIMILAR PRONOUNCIATION
 i). Knew - gnu/new - ½ Mk
 ii). Rode - road/rowed - ½ Mk
 d). i). falling
 ii). rising
 iii). Falling
 e). i). Alliteration - He who laughs last laughs best.( The sounds must be underlined)
 ii). Two characteristics
 - Figurative - It has hidden and literal meaning
 - Pithy - use few words/short /brief
 - Has two parts e.g. proposition and completion
 f). I would plan the speech by jotting and arranging points in a logical manner.
 ✓ I would rehearse before a mock audience
 ✓ I would psyche myself; yes I can.
 ✓ I would dress well (decently/formally)
 ✓ I would rehearse on pronunciation
 ✓ I would practice on voice projection
 ✓ I would carry out a pre-visit for familiarization.
 g). i). Short comings in David’s conversational skills:
 ✓ Interruption during the conversation ------what do you mean---?
 ✓ He shouts at Obuya (shouting) I did not come here to learn discipline
 ✓ Irrational in his responses (irritably) what future?
 b). What Obuya does that make the conversation successful.
 ✓ He listens attentively to David without interrupting.
 ✓ He puts himself in David’s shoes and tries to understand his position.
 ✓ He respects David’s opinions but shows why he disagrees with him.
 ✓ He uses polite language to disagree with David, “------ I am sorry ---“
 ✓ He focuses on the issues at hand and steers David from past events
 N/B 1)Student’s should not use negative response.
 2)They should not identify the traits but the shortcomings.
